title: /health is unauthenticated and returns trading state (open position count, total exposure, 24 h P&L, chain and Telegram status, version), and every hit costs one RPC call per chain

evidence.note: response body: status, version, uptime, chains (connected, latestBlock, wsConnected), positions { open, totalExposure, dailyPnL }, telegramConnected, telegramError
each request calls ctx.httpProvider.getBlockNumber() for every chain, on the same HTTP provider the exit monitors use

sibling_sites_checked: All routes mounted outside authMiddleware (server.ts:148-152, :164-177): /health (this finding), /api/auth/login (needed), the static SPA and its catch-all (no data). Every other /api route requires a session. The wording of D-20 (health unauthenticated for monitoring) covers liveness, not the money fields. Reachable cross-origin by a DNS-rebinding page (AUD-API-005) and by any network peer in remote mode.
severity_rationale: S3 EXPOSURE: discloses position count, exposure and daily P&L to anyone who can reach the port (or a rebinding page), and lets an unauthenticated client spend the shared RPC quota (one getBlockNumber per chain per request), which could rate-limit the exit quotes under a flood; no control path.
recommendation: Keep an unauthenticated liveness answer (status, chains connected) and move the position and P&L fields behind the session; cache the block-number probe for a few seconds. Card API-03. Phase 29.
